BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r2.claim: A calamity encompassed the garden at night, as the following sleep indicates; it was fire sent from heaven.

BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r3.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib defines ṭawf as circling around something to guard it, extended to a night visitor, jinn, image, or servant.

BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r4.claim: They were asleep and heedless of the decree; sleep is a light death and death heavy sleep.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r4.claim: Attributing the orchard’s destruction to God signals that the disaster arrived wholly unexpectedly and devastated it in an instant.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r1.claim: The calamity was so devastating that it miraculously reduced the orchard to nothing in a blink; ‘from your Lord’ reassures the Prophet amid Quraysh’s apparent ease.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r2.claim: The parable answers those who call the Prophet possessed because they feel secure: punishment can ruin even plans fixed by pledges when people wake to carry them out.

QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r14.claim: A calamity from heaven struck while the orchard owners slept and burned their fruits, leaving the garden like a harvested field.

FARRA:v3p174/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p174/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p174/r4.claim: God sent a fire that destroyed the garden; the sons first thought they had lost their way, then recognized that their own refusal to help the poor had brought the loss.

FARRA:v3p174/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p174/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p174/r7.claim: A طائف comes only at night; Arabs may still say أطفت بها نهارا as an idiom for an impossible or unexpected occurrence, as the poem shows.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r7.speaker: النخعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r7.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī reads طيف instead of طائف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r8.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ defines طائف as something that comes by night; Abū Ḥayyān objects that the Qur'an also uses it for satanic visitation without restricting the time.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r9.claim: One account identifies the visitor as Gabriel, who carried the uprooted garden around the Kaʿba and set it where Ṭāʾif stands; the story explains the city's name and its water, trees, and grapes.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن جرير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r10.claim: Other explanations call it God's decree, punishment from God, or a neck emerging from the Valley of Hell.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#3/r1.claim: طاف عليها means the affliction came down and encircled the orchard.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#3/r2.claim: Qatada glosses طائف as punishment, while Ibn Abbas calls it an event; al-Farra restricts a طائف to an event that comes at night.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#3/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#3/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says a tongue of fire issued from their garden valley and destroyed it.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#3/r4.claim: He rejects as unsound the story that Gabriel uprooted the orchard and carried it to the site of the city of al-Taif, as well as related relocation stories.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#3/r5.speaker: النخعي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#3/r5.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi reads طيف in place of طائف.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#4/r1.claim: من ربك means the affliction originated from God.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#4/r2.claim: وهم نائمون is circumstantial: the family were asleep, meaning the affliction reached the orchard at night, as Qatada reports.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#4/r3.claim: Alternatively, they were completely heedless of what destiny had brought upon them.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#4/r4.claim: The literal sense of sleeping at night better fits the surrounding verses.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r2.claim: A nighttime punishment visited the sleeping garden; it was fire sent from heaven that burned it.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r3.claim: A visitation from God passed over the garden while its owners slept.

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.claim: Exegetes elaborate the garden story: it belonged to a righteous man who left it to his people and town; reports place it in Yemen near Ṣanʿāʾ, Abyssinia, or among the People of Scripture.

BINTSHATI:v2p64/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p64/r3.speaker: قيل
BINTSHATI:v2p64/r3.claim: One report identifies the visitor who destroyed the garden as Satan; another identifies him as Gabriel, who uprooted and transported the trees around the Kaaba before planting them at Taif.

NAHHAS:v5p9/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p9/r16.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v5p9/r16.claim: It is said that fire was sent over the garden and burned its crops; their sleeping is a circumstantial clause.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r6.claim: The destroying visitor is a slight act for God though devastating to the orchard; the phrase from your Lord frames the punishment as merciful correction intended to reform the Prophet's people.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r7.claim: Although it is said that a taif in this sense must occur at night, the author rejects that restriction by citing a taif from Satan that touches people.

DURR-FULL:v8p251/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the visitor that passed over the garden as a command from God.

DURR-FULL:v8p251/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies the visitor as a punishment, a fiery mass from a valley of Hell.

DURR-FULL:v8p251/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r4.claim: Qatada says God's command came upon the garden at night while its owners slept, leaving it like the dark night; Qatr ibn Maymun agrees.

DURR-FULL:v8p251/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r5.claim: The Prophet warns that sin can cause lost knowledge, missed night prayer, and withheld provision, then says the owners lost their garden because of their sin.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r1.claim: طاف literally means walking around something; here it portrays the calamity as affecting the entire garden, as a specter does in 7:201.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r2.claim: The preposition على with طاف gives the sense of taking control or descending upon the garden.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r3.claim: The calamity's kind is left unnamed because its effect matters, not its type; attributing the action to a طائف functions like a passive construction.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r4.claim: Al-Farra says a طائف only comes at night, associating the word with a dream specter; Ibn Ashur questions the proposed derivation from part of the night.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r5.claim: The phrase وهم نائمون either specifies when the calamity struck or, on al-Farra's reading, reinforces the nighttime sense and depicts the scene.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r6.claim: The indefinite طائف magnifies the event; the next verse identifies it as a ruinous calamity, with a report that a fiery blast burned the garden.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r7.claim: A reported explanation says a blast of fire struck and burned the garden.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r8.claim: من ربك means sent from God: the destruction was punishment for failing to give thanks.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r9.claim: Their punishment came before they actually withheld charity because their settled resolve and oath made them culpable as if they had already withheld it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r10.claim: The passage admonishes people who do not share their wealth; the garden's worldly punishment does not prove its owners withheld obligatory zakat.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r11.claim: God sent a night visitor upon the garden, described as fire or another destructive agent, and it burned.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r22.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r22.claim: Al-Farra says طائف is an event that comes by night; the author objects that 7:201 uses the word for Satan's touch without that restriction.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336/r1.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336/r1.claim: A ṭāʾif is a visitation that occurs only by night; God's command sent a fire that burned the garden and blackened it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r3.claim: A heavenly calamity struck while they slept and left the orchard like a black night, according to Ibn Abbas, or like dry harvested stubble, according to al-Thawri and al-Suddi.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r4.claim: A Prophetic report warns that a sin can deprive a person of provision already prepared for him, and applies the warning to the garden owners’ lost crop.

JISHUMI:v10p7036/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r3.claim: The loss of the fruit may have been punishment or a trial that served as a grace, since it led them to repent.

SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r1.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r1.claim: طائف means destruction or calamity and usually signals harm; al-Farra says it is something that comes at night, but 7:201 refutes restricting it to night.

SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r2.speaker: النخعي
SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r2.claim: Al-Nakhai reads طيف; the author says this pair of descriptions was discussed at 7:201.

SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r3.claim: من ربك may attach to طاف or serve as an adjective of طائف.

SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r4.claim: الصرام is date harvesting, from a root meaning cutting; صرم and صريمة name separation and a broken-off sand tract, with Imru al-Qays and another poem illustrating the root.

SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r5.claim: Related forms mean decisive cutter, a she-camel whose milk has stopped, a month or year nearing its end, and a person whose fortune has turned bad.

SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r6.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r6.claim: الصريم may be trees stripped of fruit, night, day, or dawn; al-Shammir treats night and day as opposites named for parting from one another.

SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says الصريم is ash in the language of Khuzaima; another view takes it as a barren known sand tract in Yemen.

SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r8.speaker: في التفسير
SAMIN-DURR:68:19/r8.claim: The garden became like that; a report says it was uprooted and placed where today's Hijazi town of al-Taif stands, explaining its name.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r10.claim: The طائف that struck the garden was a command from God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r11.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r11.claim: The طائف was punishment from God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r12.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r12.claim: The طائف was a neck or column of fire that emerged from the garden's valley.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r13.claim: The visitation occurred at night while the owners slept; al-Farra says a طائف only comes by night.

MUQATIL:68:17-27/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r3.claim: A punishment from God passed over the garden at night while its owners slept.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#7/r1.claim: A calamity from God came upon the orchard while its owners slept; one report says God sent a fire that burned it.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says the destructive visitor was a command from God; Qatada calls it punishment, and Ibn Jurayj describes a fiery neck from Hell’s valley.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r12.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17-18/r12.claim: Al-Farra says a ta’if, or night visitor, comes only at night.

ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r1.claim: A heavenly punishment swept over the garden and burned all of it.

RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r1.claim: A ṭāʾif from God is a punishment that comes by night; al-Kalbī says fire came from heaven and burned the garden while its owners slept.

STUDYQURAN:68:17/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r5.claim: The visitation was a scourge sent by God.

TAB-FULL:v23p173#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p173#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p173#2/r1.claim: A divine visitor struck the garden while its owners slept; in Arabic a ṭāʾif ordinarily comes at night, though one may explicitly say it came by day.

TAB-FULL:v23p173#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p173#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p173#2/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites Abū al-Jarrāḥ's verse saying “I visited it by day, not at night,” showing that daytime visitation can be stated explicitly.

TAB-FULL:v23p173#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p173#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p173#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes the destructive visitor as an act or command from God.

TABATABAI:68:20-28/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r2.claim: A night visitation from God afflicted and surrounded the garden; it became like cut fruitless trees, a dark night after burning, or a barren patch of sand.

THALABI:v10p16/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p16/r9.claim: The visitor was a punishment that came at night, since a طائف is a night visitor; it was fire sent from heaven.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says fire surrounded and burned the orchard.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi takes عليها as referring to the orchard, which was burned by fire sent from heaven; a طائف comes only at night.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r3.speaker: أبو ظبيان عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r3.claim: Abu Zabyan transmits from Ibn Abbas that the visitor is a command from God's command.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r4.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r4.claim: Qatada says a nighttime visitor from God's command came upon the orchard; طائف means a night visitor.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r5.claim: The author says the core meaning is Ibn Abbas's explanation that fire surrounded the orchard.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:17-21/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:17-21/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:17-21/r3.claim: God sent a fire over the orchard while its owners slept and burned it.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r14.claim: While they slept, a divine command or disaster from their Lord passed around the garden on every side.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r15.claim: One report says a fire emerged from the valley where the garden stood and burned it to its roots.
